# Additions to Daniel Chapter 2 (Susanna) — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus (Theodotion recension), Additions to Daniel 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/ADD_002_page_001.jpg

---

*[Addition 2: Susanna. This is a detective story — the earliest of its kind. Two respected judges try to coerce a woman into adultery and, when she refuses, charge her with it. A young man named Daniel saves her by cross-examining them separately. The puns on tree names are intentional and untranslatable; they are preserved with notation.]*

**1** There was a man living in Babylon. His name was Joiakim.

**2** He had married a woman named Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah. She was beautiful, and she feared God.

**3** Her parents were righteous people who had raised their daughter strictly in the law of Moses.

**4** Joiakim was very wealthy, and his house had a garden attached to it. All the Jews in the area would gather there, because Joiakim was their most respected man.

**5** That year two of the elders of the community were appointed as judges. They were exactly the kind the Lord meant when he said: "Lawlessness came out from Babylon — from elder-judges who only looked like they were governing the people."

**6** These two men spent their time at the house of Joiakim. Everyone who had a legal dispute came to them.

**7** Every day at noon, after the crowds had left, Susanna would come out and walk in her husband's garden.

**8** The two elders watched her go in every single day. They watched her walk. And day by day they burned with desire for her.

**9** They let their minds go rotten. They stopped looking up at the sky. They stopped thinking about justice.

**10** Both of them were sick with longing for her — but neither one told the other.

**11** They were ashamed to admit it: they wanted to sleep with her.

**12** Still, every day, they watched and waited.

**13** One day they said to each other, "It's time to go home — it's the dinner hour." They left and went their separate ways.

**14** Then each one turned around and came back. When they ran into each other, each started pressing the other for an explanation — and both ended up admitting what they wanted. After that they put their heads together and began planning when they might catch her alone.

**15** They watched and waited for the right moment. And then one day she came into the garden the same as always, with only two maidservants. She wanted to bathe, because the day was hot.

**16** No one else was there — only the two elders, hidden and watching.

**17** Susanna said to her maidservants: "Bring me soap and oil, then close the garden doors. I want to bathe."

**18** They did exactly as she asked: they shut the garden doors and went out through the side entrances to get what they needed. They had no idea the elders were hiding there.

**19** The moment the maidservants were gone, the two elders jumped up and rushed at her.

**20** "The doors are shut," they said. "No one can see. We want you. Give in to us. Sleep with us.

**21** If you don't — we'll tell everyone we saw a young man with you, and that's why you sent your maids away."

**22** Susanna let out a groan. "I'm trapped either way. If I do this, it's death for me. If I don't, I won't get out of your hands.

**23** But I would rather fall into your hands having done nothing than sin against the Lord."

**24** And she screamed — screamed with everything she had. The two elders screamed back at her.

**25** One of them ran and threw the garden doors open.

**26** The servants heard the commotion and came running in through the side entrances to see what was happening.

**27** When the elders told them what they claimed had happened, the servants were appalled. Nothing like this had ever been said about Susanna.

**28** The next day the people gathered at Joiakim's house. The two elders arrived with murder in their hearts.

**29** They stood up before everyone and said: "Bring in Susanna, daughter of Hilkiah, the wife of Joiakim." She was sent for.

**30** She came with her father and mother, her children, and all her family.

**31** Susanna was exquisite — graceful and beautiful.

**32** The wicked elders ordered her veil removed so they could stare at her beauty.

**33** Her family and everyone who knew her were weeping.

**34** The two elders stood up in the middle of the crowd and put their hands on her head.

**35** She wept and turned her face up toward heaven. Her heart trusted the Lord.

**36** The elders testified: "We were alone in the garden when this woman came in with two maidservants. She had the doors shut and sent the maidservants away.

**37** Then a young man who had been hiding came out and slept with her.

**38** We were in the corner of the garden. When we saw what was happening, we ran toward them.

**39** We saw them together — but the man got away. He was too strong for us. He forced the doors open and ran.

**40** We grabbed the woman and demanded she tell us who the young man was.

**41** She refused. That is our testimony."

**42** The assembly believed them. They were senior judges and elders. Susanna was condemned to death.

**43** Then Susanna cried out at the top of her voice: "O eternal God — you who know what is hidden, who know everything before it happens:

**44** you know they have lied about me. And now I am going to die for things I never did — things they invented out of pure evil."

**45** The Lord heard her.

**46** As they were leading her away to be executed, God woke up the holy spirit of a young man named Daniel.

**47** He shouted out: "I will not have this woman's blood on my hands!"

**48** Everyone turned to look at him. "What did you say?"

**49** He stood in the middle of them all and said: "What is wrong with you? Are you really so stupid, people of Israel? You just condemned a daughter of Israel without a single witness being examined? Without finding out what actually happened?

**50** Get back into that court. These men lied."

**51** Everyone turned around and hurried back. The elders said to Daniel: "Come and sit with us. Tell us what you know — God has given you the standing of an elder."

**52** Daniel said: "Separate them. Put them in different places. I'm going to question them."

**53** Once they were separated, he called the first one over. He looked at him and said: "You. You who have grown old doing evil. The sins you've been committing for years have finally caught up with you.

**54** You've been giving unjust verdicts. You condemn the innocent. You let the guilty go free. And the Lord said clearly: 'You shall not put the innocent and the righteous to death.'

**55** So tell me this: if you really saw her — what tree were they under?" The elder said: "A mastic tree [schinos]." Daniel said: "That lie will cost you your life. The angel of God has his sentence ready and will cleave you in two [schizein]."

**56** He sent that one away and called the second. "You," he said. "Son of Canaan, not of Judah. Her beauty got to you. Lust twisted your judgment.

**57** You've been doing this to the daughters of Israel all along. They were too afraid to say no. But this daughter of Judah refused to go along with you.

**58** So answer me: what tree were they under?" The elder said: "A holm oak [prinos]." Daniel said: "Your lie will cost you just as much. The angel of God is waiting right now, sword in hand, to cut you in two [priein]. The two of you are finished."

**59** The whole assembly erupted. They blessed God — the God who saves those who put their hope in him.

**60** They turned on the two elders. Daniel had nailed them with their own words.

**61** They did to those men exactly what the men had tried to do to Susanna, following the law of Moses exactly. They were put to death. Innocent blood was saved that day.

**62** Hilkiah and his wife gave thanks to God for Susanna, and so did her husband Joiakim and all her family — because no shameful thing had been found in her.

**63** From that day, Daniel was a famous man among his people.

**64** Then King Astyages died and was gathered to his ancestors. Cyrus the Persian became king.
